title: Exploring Formal Logic
lines: Exploring Formal Logic introduces precise languages for examining arguments and representing knowledge.
It connects ordinary reasoning with mathematical proof, computing, and artificial intelligence.
The useful distinction is between an argument’s structure and the truth of its premises.

title: The wet street
lines: If rain makes a street wet, a wet street alone does not establish rain.
Another cause could produce the same observation.
The book turns this familiar mistake into a question about valid inference.

title: Choose the right language
lines: Propositional logic treats statements as blocks; predicates expose individuals and relationships.
Quantifiers, possibility, and time let later chapters express different kinds of questions.
A formal proof still depends on the assumptions and definitions it starts from.

title: Return to an argument
lines: Read it to make hidden assumptions visible before deciding what a conclusion warrants.
Begin with inference and truth tables, then follow the questions your problem needs.
The computing and philosophy chapters show why precision helps without replacing judgment.
